profile.headline: Robotics Technologist at Jet Propulsion Laboratory
profile.summary: Versatile problem solver with a varied skill set. Enjoys breadth as much as depth. Currently a part of JPL Robotics. Experience includes flight software on embedded Linux, ground data processing and analysis, multi-agent maritime swarm control, multi-camera systems with computer vision for maritime applications, 3D spacecraft visualization for critical event operations, teaching assistant for computational financial modeling class, visualization of JPL/NASA data, software testing on MSL, graphics programming.

positions.title: Robotics Technologist
positions.description:
- Flight software engineer for Cooperative Autonomous Distributed Robotic Exploration (CADRE) mission
- Deep clean up and refactor of Mars 2020 surface command sequence simulation software
- Refactored software for autonomous naval sea surface target control and behavior software; introduced simulation framework, automated unit tests, system tests, and report generation; performed hyper parameter optimization
- Developed detection algorithm for distant objects in maritime environment using a DCNN-based approach in PyTorch
- Cognizant engineer for maritime visual perception framework for autonomous navigation and target identification
- Ownership and modernization of wavelet image processing algorithm
- Refactored onboard processing software for BioSleeve project (hand/arm gesture detection using EMG), participated and led testing and data collection in micro gravity environment
- Hardware/software integration of camera and frame grabbing systems into image analysis framework for naval autonomy
- Lead development of discrete event simulation for multi-agent scenarios used to support multiple tasks including autonomy behavior testing and sensor fusion testing
- Developed system integration testing framework for multi-agent systems using Docker containers managed by a Python web server with configuration management, automated data handling, automated notification, and RESTful API
- Prototyped cyber security visualization and analysis tool for internal audit of Mars mission cyber vulnerabilities
- Developed live, real time, telemetry driven, visualization in support of SMAP reflector deployment critical sequences

positions.title: Staff Research Associate
positions.description: Supervised by Professor Alan L. Yuille, this position started off as a graduate student researcher until June 2014. Initial assignment was the modification of deep convolutional neural network software Caffe (written in C++) to fine tune an object detector on object window proposals. Afterward tasked with readying the lab's PASCAL Regions dataset for public release by cleaning up existing annotations. Started and managed the lab's use of work study students for human image annotations. Developed an open source tool for pixel-level image labeling with support for hierarchical layer using GIMP and Python. Created a simple website for the dataset. Developed an open source tool for shape-level image labeling using Node.js, Express, MongoDB, Mongoose.js, Backbone.js, jQuery, and D3.js.

company.name: Department of Statistics, University of California, Los Angeles

positions.title: Teaching Assistant: Management 237G Computational Methods in Finance
positions.description: Covered material on pricing options and fixed income using Monte Carlo simulation, binomial and trinomial trees, finite difference grids, and least-squares Monte Carlo. Taught by Professor Levon Goukasian.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Develop applications to visualize missions, spacecraft, and data generated by various Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA, and other space missions for dissemination internally and by the public for public outreach purposes.

Architected and developed the Eyes on the Solar System application using the Unity3D engine which involves C#/Mono development. Systems include streaming, animation, robust content frameworks, extensive content pipelines, and a custom subset implementation of ECMAScript as a custom virtual machine for a wide range of product possibilities. Also maintains project as de-facto lead using Subversion and Trac.

Developed Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Entry/Descent/Landing (EDL) visualization integrated into Eyes on the Solar System allowing for orbit-to-surface visualization of entire landing sequence.

Assisted in the development of various other projects including Eyes on the Earth, an internal Deep Space Network visualization, development of the Earth Science Center at JPL and various outreach product prototypes. Individual outreach products produced on top of this framework include: CANEO, EPOXI, Stardust NExT, Juno, GRAIL & MoonKAM, RPS, and Exoplanets.

Consulted system architecture discussions for next-generation visualization framework.

Operated visualization for NASA TV coverage of the EPOXI flyby of comet Hartley 2 and the Stardust NExT flyby of comet Tempel 1. Also operated Eyes on the Solar System's MSL EDL visualization in mission control for NASA TV coverage during landing on August 5, 2012.

Performed demos of visualization products during various events including JPL Open House, Vesta Fiesta, and Planetfest. Gave a talk at TEDxNASA@YouthDay in Hampton, Virginia on November 20, 2010. Also gave a talk at TEDxSanDiego on December 3, 2011 which was featured on the front page of TED.com and received over 200k views.

Left to pursue graduate studies full time.

positions.title: Flight System Systems Engineering Support
positions.description:
Assist flight systems systems engineering verification and validation process as an academic part-time (APT).

Performed systems testing on flight software and engineering hardware for the Mars Science Laboratory by writing testing scripts in Python that interfaced through MTAK and ran on Linux test beds. Created a testing procedure for redundancy architecture and spacecraft configuration modes.

positions.title: Graphics Programmer
positions.description:
Effects engine and tools development for unannounced project, transitioned from summer internship (2007).

Effects engine and tools development for unannounced project. Involved DirectX and shader programming in C++ and CG using Microsoft Visual Studio for the XBOX 360 platform.

Developed particle and ribbon effects as well as support effects artists. Effects were achieved with cubic hermite splines, Catmull-Rom splines and quaternion spherical interpolation. Helped to repair in-house Lua script editor/debugger using WTL and WinSock.
